pr_title: Avoid reserved characters in namer when transforming ../../
pr_body:
# ↪️ Pull Request

Tentatively fixes https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/issues/5808

Closes #6223

The issue is that some characters are considered reserved by some systems, for examples when names start with a `.` or `_`.

The namer here attempted to escape the `..` representation of a _parent directory_ by replacing the dots with underscores. `__/__/` looks close enough and is understandable, but again underscores have special meanings in some system.

I can't think of non-magic ASCII characters that aren't common letters:

- `--/--/` would be the next candidate but `--` is used for CLI flags so that could cause issues.
- `up/up/` or `parent/parent/` could work as well, but then they have a higher risk of conflict, clobbering files.

So… the closest solution is a combination of both: a short word + an uncommon character _not at the beginning_:

- `up_/up_/`

Thoughts? Alternative ideas?

## 🚨 Test instructions

I think this happens when your `index.html` uses a resource in the upper level, like `<script src="../script.js">`

## ✔️ PR Todo

- [ ] Added/updated unit tests for this change
- [x] Filled out test instructions (In case there aren't any unit tests)
- [x] Included links to related issues/PRs

issue_context.title: V2: @parcel/config-webextension: generates unacceptable folder names __
issue_context.body:
<!---
Thanks for filing an issue 😄 ! Before you submit, please read the following:

Search open/closed issues before submitting since someone might have asked the same thing before!
-->

# 🐛 bug report
Running `parcel` for devving web-extn locally (`yarn start` from `package.json` below).
If extn `manifest.json` references a file outside `src` folder, say `..assets/icon.png` - Parcel will copy that file to `dist/__/assets/icon.png`.
Pls notice the intermediary `__` folder. This is prohibited for chrome extns. When I try to load the unpackaged extn into the browser via pointing to `dist/` - it will throw this err:
`Cannot load extension with file or directory name __. Filenames starting with "_" are reserved for use by the system`

This doesn't happen when running the `build` script, mind you.
## 💻 Code Sample

`manifest.json`:
```json
{
  ...
  "browser_action": {
    "default_icon": {
      "128": "assets/icon/icon.png"
    }
  },
  "icons": {
    "128": "assets/icon/icon.png"
  }
}
```
folder structure:
```
    .
    ├── assets           
      └── icon
        └── icon.png
    ├── dist
      └── __
        └── assets
          └── icon
            └── icon.png
      └── manifest.json
      └── ...
    ├── src
      └── manifest.json
      └── ...
```


## 🎛 Configuration (.babelrc, package.json, cli command)

`.parcelrc`:
```json
{
  "extends": "@parcel/config-webextension",
  "transformers": {
    "*.{ts,tsx}": ["@parcel/transformer-typescript-tsc"]
  }
}
```
` package.json`
```json
{
  "scripts": {
    "start": "parcel src/manifest.json --host localhost --target webext-dev",
    "build": "parcel build src/manifest.json --target webext-prod",
  },
  "targets": {
    "webext-dev": {
      "sourceMap": {
        "inline": true,
        "inlineSources": true
      }
    },
    "webext-prod": {}
  },

}
```
## 🤔 Expected Behavior

Do not generate folders with chrome-restricted names


## 🌍 Your Environment

<!--- Include as many relevant details about the environment you experienced the bug in -->

| Software         | Version(s) |
| ---------------- | ---------- |
| Parcel           |  `^2.0.0-nightly.574`
| Operating System | `osX 10.14`

👉  https://opencollective.com/parcel/donate -->
comments: ~Hmm... after killing `.parcel-cache` and `dist` folders - the issue is gone. What was that about?🤔~

> Hmm... after killing `.parcel-cache` and `dist` folders - the issue is gone. What was that about?🤔

This was a mistake. I've put `assets` into `src` - because all of that it started building alright.

**So the issue is still very actively present. Please test this.**

Note: The `__` naming is actually unrelated to the web extensions transformer, but it is a breaking issue **for** web extensions.

I had the same issue and thought of an alternative "solution" (i.e. don't preserve the directory tree), but I don't know how to achieve that: https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/discussions/5858

So this occurs because the output path of the bundles is essentially `path.join(distDir, path.relative(entryRoot, entryAsset.filePath))`, and node_modules is outside of the entry root. And then the result is "sanitized" by replacing `.` with `_`.

https://github.com/parcel-bundler/parcel/blob/f28eaf60ac018d49d2176c563c86d09f84feaa8e/packages/namers/default/src/DefaultNamer.js#L123-L125
Would the solution here be to just drop any `../` instead of sanitizing them? Or what do you suggest?

You could run into a naming collision with that, e.g.: ``` src/index.html src/src2/test.html src2/test.html ``` and `src/index.html` being ```html X X ``` would right now create: ``` dist/index.html dist/src2/test.html dist/__/src2/test.html ```

```
dist/index.html
dist/src2/test.html
dist/__/src2/test.html
```

would have to become

```
dist/index.html
dist/src2/test.html
dist/src2/test.717dcb8d.html
```

Linking to `..` would not make sense for public URLs anyway, so renaming the second `test.html` would be an alternative
No, the contract for `bundle.isEntry` is not adding a hash.

Perhaps we could use `$` instead of `_` to prevent naming collisions. I don't think there are too many things that depend on `$` (besides maybe shell variables, but realistically nobody will be running a shell script on Parcel output). Alternatively, the solution in #5893 doesn't seem too bad to me...

We could also replace `__` with something like `dist`. Doesn't look as odd the various proposals involving different punctuation.

Do you want to open a new PR similar to the one you linked? Picking a different name other than `__` would certainly be a fine workaround for this issue

I think it's a good idea to indicate somehow that a `..` was replaced somehow. Actually, I think #5893 should just be merged, since it seems to be a good-enough solution to this problem. I could recreate it, but realistically the use of `up_` is quite nice (the alternative is something like `bk_`).

Someone has to recreate it, I can't reopen it because the branch was deleted

![Bildschirmfoto 2021-05-02 um 23 10 37](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4586894/116827852-9c919800-ab9b-11eb-82e9-96ed6459c2d4.png)
I reopened my PR since it has more context, if you're interested in merging it.
